title: TRUNCATE TABLE
description: Learn how to use TRUNCATE TABLE to remove all rows from a table faster and more efficiently than DELETE.

data.text: The TRUNCATE TABLE statement removes all rows from a table faster and more efficiently than the DELETE statement without a WHERE clause.

data.title: TRUNCATE TABLE Syntax
data.content: Removes all rows from the specified table.

data.text: The database name is optional. If omitted, the statement truncates the table in the currently connected database.
TRUNCATE TABLE has several advantages over DELETE without a WHERE clause:

The DELETE statement removes rows one at a time and inserts an entry in the transaction log for each removed row. TRUNCATE TABLE deallocates the data pages used to store the table data and inserts only the page deallocations in the transaction logs.
When DELETE is executed using a row lock, each row in the table is locked for removal. TRUNCATE TABLE locks the table and pages, not each row individually.
If the table has an identity column, TRUNCATE TABLE resets the counter to the seed value. DELETE without a WHERE clause does not reset the identity counter.

data.title: TRUNCATE TABLE Example
data.content: Creates a customer_groups table, inserts rows, then truncates it.

data.title: TRUNCATE TABLE Key Points
points: TRUNCATE TABLE removes all rows faster than DELETE without WHERE.
It uses less transaction log space by deallocating data pages.
It uses fewer locks by locking the table and pages instead of each row.
It resets the identity column counter to the seed value.
TRUNCATE cannot be used on tables referenced by a FOREIGN KEY constraint.
